name: #BlackTechFutures Research Institute
description: Builds national network of HBCUs, city-based researchers, and community institutions focused on local Black tech ecosystems and tech talent. Received PIT Fund support to bolster Black civic tech workforce pipeline.
funding_detail: Public Interest Tech Fund ($250K grant) + philanthropic

name: All Tech Is Human
description: Responsible tech advocacy org. Slack community, job board, and mentorship program connecting people to careers in public interest technology. Focuses on diversifying the pipeline into tech policy and civic tech roles.

name: Alliance of Civic Technologists (ACT)
description: National umbrella connecting 18+ volunteer civic tech groups. Organizes CityCamp unconferences and Civic Spark convenings. 500+ Discord members.

name: Civic Tech Field Guide
description: World's largest collection of civic tech projects and organizations. Field Guide Friday newsletter (4,300+ subscribers). Open resource cataloguing the global civic tech ecosystem. Key discovery tool for technologists entering the field.

name: Demand Progress
description: Progressive advocacy org with dedicated congressional modernization portfolio. Advocates for transparency, open data, and strengthening legislative branch capacity. Co-authored bipartisan House rules reform proposals with Lincoln Network. Tracks legislative data and capacity issues.

name: Federation of American Scientists (FAS)
description: Nonpartisan think tank running Day One Project for policy entrepreneurship. Innovation Ecosystem Job Board for displaced federal technologists (2025). Senior Fellows program.
funding_detail: Schmidt Futures, Open Philanthropy, broad base

name: GovAI Coalition
description: Coalition of 2,000+ public servants from 700+ local, county, and state governments advocating for responsible public sector AI. Historically led by City of San Jose, but transitioned to full non-profit status. Produces AI policy templates, vendor AI FactSheets, use case libraries, and AI Contract Hub. Open to government, academia, and industry.
funding_detail: City of San Jose leads; member contributions; philanthropic support

name: Inclusive Abundance / Abundance Network
description: Coalition advocating for abundance-agenda policy: housing, energy, permitting reform, state capacity. Members include FAS, Niskanen, R Street, New America.

name: National Conference on Citizenship (NCoC) / Project Redesign
description: Civic health research. Project Redesign focuses on redesigning public services. Co-created TELI program.

name: Open The Government
description: Coalition advocating for government transparency, open data, and accountability. Works on FOIA reform, open data policy, and government information access. Part of broader good-government advocacy ecosystem.

name: Partnership for Public Service
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit advocating for effective federal government. Produces Best Places to Work rankings, leadership development programs, and tech modernization policy recommendations.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; earned revenue from training

name: POPVOX Foundation
description: Leads congressional modernization advocacy. Published 'Future-Proofing Congress' resources. Co-organizes Congressional Hackathon (7th edition 2025). Advocates for legislative data transparency, AI adoption in Congress, and open-source civic tech tools for the legislative branch.
funding_detail: Hewlett Foundation, Democracy Fund, philanthropic grants

name: Public Interest Technology University Network (PIT-UN)
description: Network of 63 universities co-convened by New America, Ford Foundation, and Hewlett Foundation. $16M+ deployed to 154 projects building the PIT field through curriculum, faculty research, and experiential learning.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Mastercard, McGovern, Raikes, Schmidt Futures, Siegel

name: Recoding America Fund
description: $120M 6-year pooled philanthropic initiative grantmaking for government workforce, digital infrastructure, and procedural reform. Chaired by Jennifer Pahlka.
funding_detail: Pooled fund; inaugural donors not yet fully public

name: Results for America
description: Helps government use evidence and data. Runs What Works Cities and States certifications promoting performance management and evidence-based policymaking.

name: Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP): AI Expo / Talent Initiatives
description: Eric Schmidt-founded initiative (2022) focused on maintaining U.S. technological competitiveness in AI and advanced technology vis-a-vis strategic competitors. Produces policy recommendations, convenes government and industry leaders, and hosts the annual AI Expo for National Competitiveness in DC. Not a fellowship program - included for its role in shaping AI talent policy and government-technology workforce discussions.

name: Tech Talent Project
description: Bridges technologists and government hiring. Co-runs TELI executive training with Aspen Policy Academy. Improves government tech recruitment practices.

name: BetaNYC
description: NYC's civic tech, open data, and open government community (est. 2013). Co-hosts NYC Open Data Week and NYC School of Data (600+ attendees). Builds tools like Boundaries Map. Partners with NYC Office of Technology & Innovation. ACT founding member.
funding_detail: Small grants; NYC OTI partnership; volunteer-driven

name: Chi Hack Night
description: Chicago's weekly civic tech meetup (est. 2012). In-person and online hack nights featuring speakers from government, nonprofits, and tech. Spawned projects like mRelief (food stamps access). Elected board; ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech Atlanta
description: Atlanta civic tech group hosting monthly hack nights. Provides data support to community organizations (e.g., Sanctuary Food Pantry). Active project lifecycle pipeline. ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech DC
description: Washington DC volunteer civic hacking group. Hosted Civic Hack DC 2025 (80 participants) focused on open-source tools for Regulations.gov public comment analysis. ACT member.

name: Code for Boston
description: Boston-area civic innovation group. Semi-weekly hybrid hack nights at Cambridge Innovation Center. Building MAPLE (Massachusetts Platform for Legislative Engagement) enabling residents to submit legislative testimony. ACT founding member.

name: Code for BTV
description: Burlington, VT civic tech group hosting biweekly 'Action Nights' (fmr. Hack Night). ACT founding member.

name: Code for Charlottesville
description: Charlottesville, VA civic tech group working with local nonprofits and government agencies on pro bono tech projects. Active GitHub presence through 2025 (Virginia Schools AI policy analysis, native plants DB, Meals on Wheels portal). UVA and PVCC student involvement. ACT member.

name: Code for Dayton
description: Dayton civic tech group with monthly meetings. Projects include Florence Nightingale Museum website and demolition permit monitoring for Preservation Dayton. ACT founding member.

name: Code for Philly
description: Philadelphia civic tech community. Building Clean & Green Philly (toolkit for reducing gun violence via vacant lot greening) and Phlask (map of free water/food/bathrooms). Benefit Decision Toolkit for eligibility screeners. ACT founding member.

name: Code with the Carolinas
description: Carolinas civic tech community. Active through 2024 on Open Sidewalks (sidewalk accessibility mapping) and Zoning Atlas projects. Completed transition from Code for America Brigade Network in 2023. Fiscally sponsored through Open Collective. ACT member.

name: ELGL (Engaging Local Government Leaders)
description: 501(c)(3) connecting innovative local government leaders. 4,800+ members across all 50 states. Runs GovLove Podcast, Top Influencers awards, Analyst Academy, and Public Service Recognition Week. Key community for local gov professionals seeking peers.

name: Florida Community Innovation (FCI)
description: Florida civic tech organization. Published organizational handbook (2025). Florida Resource Map project. AI Fellow program. ACT member.

name: GovLoop
description: Online community of 300,000+ government professionals. Featured Contributor Program, NextGen Government Training Summit, and educational resources on modernization, AI, and workforce. Knowledge-sharing platform connecting public servants across levels.
funding_detail: GovExec Media / Owned by Government Executive Media Group; sponsor-supported content

name: Hack for LA
description: Los Angeles network of civic-minded technologists building digital products with community partners and local government. Global volunteer base (designers, developers, PMs). Maintains Civic Tech Index.

name: Open Austin
description: Austin civic tech community hosting design community of practice, hack nights, and mixers. Sold-out 2025 Public Interest Tech Mixer (37 attendees, 40% people of color). ACT founding member.

name: Open Sacramento
description: Sacramento civic tech group (recently rebranded with new website). Virtual community action nights. ACT member.

name: Open Source San Jose
description: San Jose civic tech collective (joined ACT 2025). Monthly hack nights. Building Tally Up app for CA Dept of Education meal distribution tracking. Open-source, community-driven innovation.

name: OpenOakland
description: Oakland civic tech group building tools for government transparency and community access. ACT member.

name: SF Civic Tech
description: San Francisco civic tech community (fmr. Code for San Francisco, est. 2013). Weekly virtual hack nights. Building SafeHome earthquake risk dashboard. Independent 501(c)(3) since 2024. ACT founding member.

name: Technologists for the Public Good (TPG)
description: 501(c)(6) professional association (est. 2020) for technologists working across government, nonprofits, academia, philanthropy, and civic tech. 134% membership growth in 2023. Runs networking events, tech and design conferences, mentorship programs, and the Tech to Gov Virtual Forum & Job Fair connecting senior technologists with government agencies. Joint statement with ACT on civic tech field direction (2025). Co-hosted State of GovTech 2025 with CivStart in Arlington. Members include government digital service alumni, current federal and state tech staff, and public interest tech practitioners.

name: UChicago Civic Analytics Network (Harris School)
description: Network of chief data officers and analytics leaders in government. Research on data-driven governance and performance management.

name: AAAS S&T Policy Fellowships
description: 1-2 year fellowships placing scientists and engineers in federal agencies and Congress. Expanded AI tracks. 3,500+ alumni since 1973.

name: Bloomberg Harvard City Hall Fellows
description: Places emerging leaders (recent graduates + mid-career) in city halls to work on data, innovation, and performance management. Fellows embedded in mayor's offices working on priority challenges. Distinct from the City Leadership Initiative exec education.

name: California Capital Fellows Program
description: Four fellowships (Assembly, Senate, Executive, Judicial) placing 64 fellows/year at highest levels of CA state government for 10-11 months. Fellows assist legislators, senior executive staff, and court administrators on policy. Nationally recognized.

name: CITP Technology Fellows (Princeton)
description: Non-resident fellowship connecting experienced gov technologists to state/local regulatory challenges in AI governance, data privacy, and cybersecurity.

name: CivicSpark (AmeriCorps)
description: 11-month AmeriCorps fellowship placing ~150 fellows/year in local governments and community orgs for capacity building on climate, housing, water, transportation, public health. 1,000+ alumni since 2014. Expanding beyond CA/CO/WA to all states starting 2025.
funding_detail: AmeriCorps federal funding + local agency cost-share ($37,500/fellow)

name: Coding it Forward Fellowship
description: 10-week paid summer placement of early-career technologists in federal, state, and local government. Five tracks: data, design, product, software, cybersecurity. 700+ alumni.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment, McGovern Foundation, Pivotal Ventures

name: Cornell Tech PiTech Initiative
description: PhD Impact Fellowships, Visiting Practitioner's Program, and PiTech Impact Studio for graduate students working on public interest technology.

name: Coro Fellows Program in Public Affairs
description: 7-9 month full-time experiential leadership program. Fellows rotate through placements in government, nonprofit, business, and labor. 80+ year track record. 15,000+ alumni including US Senators and elected officials. Programs in LA, SF, NYC, Pittsburgh, St. Louis.

name: DC Capital City Fellows Program (CCFP)
description: 18-month mayoral initiative placing recent masters graduates in DC government agencies. Three 6-month rotations across government operations, health/human services, public safety, planning, or education. Entry salary ~$62K.

name: FUSE Corps
description: 1-year executive fellowship placing experienced professionals in city/county agencies for strategic projects. 250+ projects across 42 cities/18 states.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Irvine Foundation

name: Georgetown Beeck Center Innovation + Incubation Fellowship
description: 12-24 month fellowship for senior subject matter experts in data, design, technology, and policy. Fellows publish research, document best practices, and push the field forward. Current fellow focused on AI + public interest technology. Expanding to more states in 2026.

name: Georgetown McCourt Tech & Policy Visiting Fellows
description: Semester-long visiting fellowship for tech policy practitioners at Georgetown McCourt School. Multiple USDS alumni and former federal tech officials in inaugural 2025 cohort. Fellows write policy essays, mentor students, and conduct research.

name: Govern for America (GFA)
description: Two-year paid fellowship placing recent graduates in high-impact state/local government roles. Published AI x Talent research for states.

name: Harvard Ash Center Democracy Fellowships
description: Financial support for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers studying democratic governance, innovation in government, and civic technology. Part of the Ash Center's Program on Democratic Governance.

name: Horizon Institute for Public Service
description: Training and fellowships for scientists and technologists entering government service.

name: Judicial Innovation Fellowship (Georgetown)
description: 1-year fellowship placing technologists, designers, and user testers in state, local, tribal, and territorial courts to build data infrastructure, simplify processes, and improve access to justice. Inaugural cohort 2023-24. Incubated at Georgetown Law's Institute for Technology Law & Policy.

name: Media Democracy Fund Fellowships
description: Technology Exchange (12+ months at civil society orgs) and PhDX Fellowship (PhD students at DC policy orgs). Focused on public interest technology and media policy.

name: NobleReach Scholars (NobleReach Foundation)
description: 1-2 year fully compensated fellowship placing early-career technologists (AI, cybersecurity, business process innovation) in federal, state, and local government roles. Launched 2024; 19 scholars in inaugural cohort, 28 in 2025 cohort (selected from 1,200+ applicants). Expanded in April 2025 to include state and local government placements alongside federal. NobleReach named founding partner of OPM's U.S. Tech Force (Dec 2025). $400M+ endowment (proceeds from divestiture of LMI Consulting). Strong national security framing but meaningful state capacity placements - 2025 cohort placed at Oklahoma City, Pittsburgh, Miami-Dade Innovation Authority, Maryland DoIT, and Montgomery County PA AI Council.
funding_detail: $400M+ endowment from LMI Consulting divestiture; fellows receive full salary + $15K stipend

name: Paragon Policy Fellowship
description: Connects university students and recent graduates with technology policy and digital governance work.

name: S&T Impact: State Legislative Futures Forum
description: Partnership with TechCongress to extend tech policy fellowship model to state legislatures. Inaugural State Legislative Futures Forum held in DC 2025. Trains technologists on state-level policymaking.

name: TechCongress
description: 1-year fellowship placing technologists as policy advisors in Congressional offices and committees. Bipartisan placements.
funding_detail: Hewlett Foundation, Omidyar Network, Ford Foundation

name: xD (U.S. Census Bureau)
description: Emerging technology fellowship for mid-career technologists at Census Bureau focused on AI/ML, data engineering, and emerging tech.

name: 18F (GSA)
description: Eliminated March 2025. Was GSA internal consultancy providing agile development, procurement consulting, user research, and open-source tooling to federal agencies. Open-source resources redeployed externally by alumni.

name: Arizona Strategic Enterprise Technology Office (ADOA-ASET)
description: Statewide IT strategy and digital services division within the Arizona Department of Administration, led by State CIO J.R. Sloan. Closed 90 on-premises data centers via a cloud-first policy, migrated 2,900+ applications, and increased online services available to Arizonans by 250% in two years. Operates a dedicated Office of Digital Solutions managing 200+ state agency websites and enterprise applications including Business One Stop. Earned A- overall and first place in resilience on the 2024 Center for Digital Government Digital States Survey.
funding_detail: AZ state general fund; Web Portal Fund; ADOA automation operations fund

name: Arlington County Digital Innovation
description: County digital innovation division with 7+ year AI program. Operates virtual assistant 'Ava', enterprise data warehouse, and open-source ML tools.

name: ARPA-H
description: Funds high-risk, high-reward health research via ARPA model: empowered program managers, milestone-based funding, other transaction authority. ~$1.5B annual budget.

name: Austin Office of Design & Delivery
description: Municipal digital services team providing service design, user research, content strategy, and digital forms for city services.

name: BIA Indigenous Connectivity and Technology Division
description: Division within the Bureau of Indian Affairs Office of Trust Services providing technical assistance to Tribal Nations on broadband, electromagnetic spectrum leasing, wireless services, and digital capacity on tribal lands. Established 2022-2023 to give Tribal Nations a formal seat in national connectivity policy development and support their sovereignty over digital resources and telecommunications infrastructure. Coordinates with FCC, NTIA, and Commerce Dept on tribal broadband priorities. Administers tribal components of the National Spectrum Strategy Implementation Plan. Note: created under the Biden administration; archived content as of Jan 20, 2025 - current operational status under review.

name: Boston Department of Innovation and Technology (DoIT)
description: City of Boston's enterprise technology organization serving 18,000+ city employees and hundreds of thousands of constituents. In May 2025 the Boston City Council codified DoIT into city law, granting it formal authority over citywide technology procurement, cybersecurity, and data governance. Manages BOS:311, digital services delivery, the Wicked Free Wi-Fi program, and a Digital Equity Fund. ~150 employees under Mayor Michelle Wu's Innovation and Technology Cabinet.
funding_detail: City of Boston budget; federal digital equity grants (MBI Partnership Grant)

name: California Office of Data & Innovation (ODI)
description: Statewide digital services team delivering user research, content design, data analytics, and plain language guidance across CA state agencies.

name: Chicago Department of Technology and Innovation (DTI)
description: New citywide technology department established under Mayor Brandon Johnson (est. late 2023) - a deliberate rethinking of Chicago's IT approach. CIO/Commissioner Nick Lucius confirmed by City Council 48-0 in May 2024. Lucius previously served as Chicago's chief data officer and CTO. Maintains the Chicago Design System and coordinates technology across all city departments under a unified strategy focused on reducing operational complexity and improving resident-facing digital service delivery.

name: City and County of Denver - Peak Academy & Technology Services
description: Denver leads in two distinct dimensions of city capacity. Denver Peak Academy (within the Budget & Management Office) has trained 11,000+ Denver employees and participants from 350+ governments in lean process improvement since 2012, saving the city $75M+. Alongside it, the Office of Information Technology (OIT) drives digital modernization including an Automation Center of Excellence that won Colorado Technology Association's 2024 Apex Project of the Year and saved $2.9M and 54,000 staff hours. OIT recently created separate CDO and CISO roles under CIO Suma Nallapati.
funding_detail: City and County of Denver general fund

name: CODE PA
description: State digital delivery team (~50 staff) created 2023 under Gov. Shapiro. Delivers human-centered design, accessibility, and digital service improvements across PA agencies.

name: Colorado Digital Service
description: State digital team founded by USDS alumni. Enterprise approach to modernizing resident experience using agile, user research, and product management.

name: Georgia Office of Artificial Intelligence
description: Dedicated state AI office. Published AI Roadmap and Governance Framework. $15M additional for cybersecurity/AI. Cloud-first initiative with AI integration.

name: Gilbert, AZ Office of Digital Government
description: City digital government office delivering social media strategy, open data, civic engagement, and digital innovation. Nationally recognized.

name: Illinois Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT)
description: State enterprise IT agency created by statute in 2018, serving 36 client agencies directly and 90+ government entities statewide including high-speed broadband to 610 school districts. Led by State CIO/Secretary Sanjay Gupta (former USDOJ and SBA CIO; Senate-confirmed 2024). Key 2024-25 initiatives include enterprise AI governance, benefits modernization for SNAP and Medicaid, digital driver's licenses via Apple Wallet, and a new Central Computing Facility replacing 1970s-era legacy data center infrastructure.

name: InnovateOhio Platform (Ohio Office of Information Technology)
description: Ohio's enterprise digital modernization initiative within the Department of Administrative Services' Office of Information Technology, led by State CIO Katrina Flory (GovTech Top 25 2024). Delivers OH|ID statewide single sign-on (used by nearly half of all Ohioans), data analytics, fraud detection, and a new content management system across hundreds of agency websites and apps. Added digital driver's licenses to Apple Wallet in 2024. Received NASCIO State IT Recognition Award for cybersecurity excellence in 2025.

name: Lebanon, NH
description: Small city with dedicated Chief Innovation & AI Officer. AI policy, procurement, training. Serves on NH AI Task Force.

name: Los Angeles Information Technology Agency (ITA)
description: City of LA's enterprise technology department - 442 IT professionals across 18 divisions delivering 366 services on a $90M annual operating budget. Led by General Manager and CIO Ted Ross. Ranked #1 Digital City nationally in 2023 and #2 in 2024 by the Center for Digital Government. Published Los Angeles A.I. Roadmap (June 2024) and 2024-2025 Strategic Plan focused on digital transformation, AI governance, and smart city infrastructure for the 2026 World Cup, 2027 Super Bowl, and 2028 Olympics.
funding_detail: City of LA general fund; operating + capital budget appropriations

name: Maryland Digital Service & Office of AI Enablement
description: Digital service and AI delivery arm of the Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT) operating under Gov. Wes Moore's executive modernization mandate. Launched a bilingual AI chatbot (Claude Sonnet) serving 600K+ residents for SUN Bucks food benefits. Co-leading a landmark multi-agency AI partnership with Anthropic and Percepta - backed by Rockefeller Foundation - to modernize benefits delivery, environmental permitting, and housing access. Published 2025 AI Enablement Strategy and AI Study Roadmap covering 12 critical domains.
funding_detail: MD state general fund; Anthropic/Percepta partnership; Rockefeller Foundation support

name: Massachusetts Digital Service (Mass Digital)
description: State digital service team within the Executive Office of Technology Services & Security (EOTSS). Implements the Commonwealth Digital Roadmap - a multi-year plan for accessible people-centered digital experiences across all MA agencies. Built MyMassGov single sign-on (1.5M+ users) and the 'Ask MA' multilingual chatbot (700K+ monthly users); announced deployment of ChatGPT to all 40K executive branch employees in 2026. Authorized by Gov. Healey's FutureTech Act of 2024 ($110M bond authorization). Ranked #1 in the nation by the Center for Digital Government's GovX Awards in 2024.
funding_detail: MA state general fund + $110M FutureTech Act bond authorization

name: Minnesota IT Services (MNIT)
description: Enterprise IT agency for Minnesota's executive branch serving 70+ agencies, 375+ partners, and 87 counties. Active transformation program: launched LoginMN (centralized single sign-on), hired the state's first AI Director, deployed $13.1M through the Technology Modernization Fund in 2024, and migrated 50%+ of servers to cloud. Published 2024 and 2025 annual impact reports documenting 33+ new or enhanced self-service tools. The Technology Advisory Council (TAC) provides cross-sector governance guidance on AI, customer experience, and product-driven IT delivery.
funding_detail: State IT enterprise fund (chargeback model) + MN general fund appropriations

name: New Hampshire Department of Information Technology (DoIT)
description: Centralized state IT agency led by Commissioner/CIO Denis Goulet (NASCIO Decade of Leadership Award 2025; NASCIO President 2020) - one of the few CIOs to serve across three governors. Redesigned all state websites and apps for constituent usability; launched a statewide business portal; built the VINI vaccine registration system during COVID-19; and launched '.Gov In a Box' providing funding and contractor support to help local governments migrate to .gov domains. Pursuing whole-of-state cybersecurity and agile/MVP methodologies with agency partners.
funding_detail: NH state general fund + federal SLCGP cybersecurity grants

name: New Jersey Office of Innovation
description: State innovation office (~50+ staff) building digital products (Business.NJ.gov, NJ AI Assistant) and providing product management, human-centered design, and data science to NJ agencies.

name: New York State (ITS)
description: NY Office of Information Technology Services. Among 17+ states with official digital service teams per Beeck Center. Partnership with InnovateUS rolling out AI to 100K+ city employees.

name: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI)
description: New York City's consolidated technology agency formed in 2022 by merging DoITT, the Mayor's Office of the CTO, NYC Cyber Command, the Mayor's Office of Data Analytics, and the Mayor's Office of Information Privacy. Led by CTO Lisa Gelobter (2026). Employs ~1,200 staff with an operating budget of ~$350M and capital budget of ~$1B. Administers NYC311 (175+ languages), leads the MyCity resident portal, manages the city's open data program (2,000+ datasets), and coordinates digital equity and broadband expansion.

name: OPM Data Science Fellows
description: New cross-agency fellowship launched Dec 2025 by OPM to fill critical data science skills gaps in federal agencies. Part of OPM's suite of new technology talent programs replacing the terminated Presidential Management Fellows program. Fellows are hired by and onboarded at individual agencies, with OPM providing central administration and skills-based assessment. Initial pilot cohorts launching spring 2026.
funding_detail: Federal agency appropriations; centrally administered by OPM

name: OPM Project Management Fellows
description: New cross-agency fellowship launched Dec 2025 by OPM to fill longstanding project management skills gaps. Part of OPM's suite of new technology talent programs replacing the terminated Presidential Management Fellows program. Fellows hired at individual agencies; OPM provides central administration, assessment, and oversight. Initial pilot cohorts launching spring 2026.
funding_detail: Federal agency appropriations; centrally administered by OPM

name: Philadelphia Digital Services
description: City digital team providing UX research, content strategy, and digital form development using USWDS.

name: Portland Digital Services (BTS)
description: Digital services team delivering human-centered design and plain language improvements. Won 2025 USDR Innovation in Constraints award.

name: Presidential Innovation Fellows (PIF)
description: Embeds mid-to-senior technologists (GS-15) in federal agencies for 12-month tours providing product management, AI strategy, design, and engineering advisory. 260+ alumni.

name: San Francisco Digital and Data Services (DDS)
description: Human-centered digital service team within the City Administrator's office. Manages SF.gov - the unified city web platform with 80+ departments migrated - applying equitable design standards, plain language requirements, and the City's Language Access Ordinance. Launched an Emerging Technologies team in November 2024 that piloted ChatGPT Enterprise with OpenAI and deployed Microsoft Copilot Chat to 30,000 city staff, establishing SF as a national leader in public sector AI adoption.
funding_detail: City and County of San Francisco budget; COIT Major IT Project Allocation

name: San Jose Innovation & IT
description: City innovation team running data governance, AI strategy development, and employee upskilling. Leads GovAI coalition.

name: Seattle Information Technology (Seattle IT)
description: City of Seattle's enterprise technology department led by CTO Rob Lloyd (appointed 2024). Employs 633+ staff with an operating budget of ~$280M. Published 2025-2027 Strategic Plan anchoring technology to public safety, housing, health, and economic opportunity. Launched Eproval (modern permitting platform), the One Seattle Data Strategy (city's first comprehensive data governance plan), and CiviformX (one-stop portal for affordability programs). Longstanding digital equity program including Technology Matching Fund grants spanning 30+ years.
funding_detail: City of Seattle general fund + capital budget

name: U.S. Digital Corps
description: Two-year early-career federal fellowship in software engineering, data science, product, design, and cybersecurity. 150+ fellows; 95% convert to career positions.

name: U.S. DOGE Service (fmr. USDS)
description: Renamed from U.S. Digital Service; reorganized under DOGE. ~20 legacy staff from 200+. Runs software modernization projects; original user-centered digital delivery mission shifted. Temp org expires Jul 4 2026.

name: U.S. Tech Force (OPM)
description: New cross-agency technology fellowship launched Dec 2025 by OPM, explicitly positioned as the replacement for the terminated Presidential Management Fellows program. Annual cohorts of 1,000 fellows in AI, cybersecurity, data science, and software engineering placed across federal agencies in 1-2 year positions. Large agencies to receive teams of 30-40 fellows. Pilot cohort spring 2026; full implementation by Sept 2026. NobleReach Foundation named as a founding partner.
funding_detail: Federal agency appropriations; centrally administered by OPM

name: Utah Digital Government
description: Pioneer in digital government. Digital ID adopted by 40K in 3 months. Personalized citizen portal across agencies. Cybersecurity support to 100+ local entities.

name: Washington Technology Solutions (WaTech)
description: Washington State's central IT agency leading the Digital Experience program including a Resident Portal roadmap for unified digital access across agencies, an AI Community of Practice, the state's first-ever Enterprise Privacy and Data Protection Policy, and AI Procurement Guidelines for legislative decision-making. Developed 16 new government websites in 2024. Published 2024-2026 strategic plan; new CTO Gretchen Peri appointed September 2025.
funding_detail: WA state general fund + federal State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program funds

name: 8VC (Joe Lonsdale)
description: Venture capital firm with explicit govtech and defense tech investment thesis. Co-founded and backed OpenGov (acquired by Cox Enterprises for $1.8B in 2024). American Dynamism practice includes government software, defense, and infrastructure startups. Lonsdale is a prominent advocate for government modernization through private-sector technology.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $6B+ AUM across multiple funds

name: Advantage Capital / InState Partners
description: St. Louis-based impact investor with InState Partners as a dedicated govtech business line (est. 2013). Combines investment capital with a proprietary 50-state government affairs network to help startups navigate procurement. First investor in PayIt; portfolio includes multiple state and local govtech companies. Three-year strategic partnership with CivStart to accelerate govtech funding. Has deployed $4B+ total across all funds.
funding_detail: Tax credit-driven funds + traditional LP capital; $4B+ total deployed; InState Partners is dedicated govtech line

name: Andreessen Horowitz
description: Major VC with govtech portfolio primarily through American Dynamism practice targeting defense and government technology startups. Notable govtech investments include OpenGov ($1.8B exit to Cox Enterprises, 2024), Flock Safety ($658M raised, $7.5B valuation), and Skydio. Govtech is a meaningful but not exclusive focus - defense and national security dominate the American Dynamism portfolio.
funding_detail: LP-funded; $42B+ AUM; American Dynamism Fund dedicated to defense and government tech

name: BarronKent Ventures
description: Sacramento-based family office and early-stage VC fund with an explicit and deep govtech focus - founded by principals with 18 years running a national GovTech consulting firm before transitioning to investing. Invests in early and growth-stage companies across govtech, healthcare technology, and digital services. Markets served include health and human services, transportation/tolling, licensing and regulatory, and accounting/financial systems. Active participant in CivStart ecosystem and State of GovTech convenings.
funding_detail: Family office + LP-funded VC; undisclosed fund size; early to growth stage

name: BV Investment Partners
description: Boston-based middle-market PE firm with a deliberate govtech investment thesis. Made initial minority investment in CivicPlus in 2019 - a local government website and citizen engagement platform - scaling it before its $290M exit to Insight Partners in 2021. Government technology is a named sector focus alongside tech-enabled business services.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; ~$3.9B total invested since 1983; govtech is named sector focus

name: Commonweal Ventures
description: Early-stage VC fund investing in technology companies serving government customers with a focus on public safety and state/local government. Portfolio includes Multitude Insights (law enforcement collaboration tools), Deckard Technologies (AI-driven municipal tax compliance), and others serving SLED markets. Participated in Starbridge Series A (2025).
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; undisclosed fund size; seed and early-stage focus on public safety and govtech

name: Govtech Fund (Ron Bouganim)
description: First venture capital fund dedicated exclusively to government technology startups, founded by Ron Bouganim. Makes seed-stage investments ($250K-$500K) in companies selling technology directly to government. ~$50M across two funds. Portfolio includes Mark43 (public safety), SeamlessDocs/GovOS (digital forms), SmartProcure (procurement intelligence), and Merit (verified credentials). Bouganim serves on board of Merit. Strong NASCIO and govtech conference presence.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; ~$50M AUM across two funds; seed stage ($250K-$500K checks)

name: Govtech Ventures (Rachel Stern)
description: Early-stage VC fund (est. 2024) dedicated exclusively to modernizing state and local government. Founded by Rachel Stern, who was the first investor in PayIt and co-founded InState Partners at Advantage Capital. Raising a $15M inaugural fund targeting pre-seed through seed-plus with LPs including govtech founders and family offices. Portfolio includes Polco, Streamline, and Ladris. Focused specifically on SLED market operators.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; ~$15M inaugural fund (fundraising 2024-2025); pre-seed to seed-plus stage

name: Great Hill Partners
description: Boston-based PE firm that built a deliberate govtech investment strategy. Hired Granicus co-founder Tom Spengler as Executive-in-Residence to source govtech deals. In 2025 led the majority recapitalization of Vision Government Solutions - property tax and appraisal software serving 900+ jurisdictions - alongside Weatherford Capital. Strong track record of govtech platform investments and exits.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; $12B+ total capital raised across funds; govtech is named vertical

name: Kapor Capital
description: Oakland-based early-stage VC (est. 1999) investing in tech startups that close gaps of access for low-income communities and communities of color. Notable govtech investments include Promise (government payment modernization) and Aclima (air quality monitoring for regulators and municipalities). $224M+ AUM across multiple funds. Co-founder Mitchell Kapor is a longtime civic tech philanthropist. Portfolio of 170+ active investments with 4 unicorns and 6 IPOs.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $224M+ AUM; Kapor Capital Fund III; seed stage focus

name: Omidyar Network
description: Philanthropic investment firm that makes both grants and equity investments at the intersection of responsible technology and governance. Funds TechCongress and responsible technology initiatives with an explicit focus on ensuring the digital revolution serves shared power and prosperity. Has deployed $2B+ to 700+ organizations spanning nonprofits and for-profits. Spun out Luminate (grants) and retained the investing arm as Omidyar Network.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar personal capital; ~$2B deployed across grants and equity investments

name: Serent Capital
description: Growth-focused PE firm with a dedicated GovTech investment team. Five govtech platform investments in four years including BS&A Software (municipal ERP, acquired 2021), First Due (fire and EMS software), GovWorx (911 quality assurance), and Pondera Solutions (fraud detection for government benefits, exited to Thomson Reuters). Targets profitable, recurring-revenue cloud SaaS companies selling to state and local agencies.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; multiple funds since 2008; $3B+ total capital under management

name: Socium Ventures
description: Evergreen venture fund backed by Cox Enterprises with $600M+ committed across two funds (Fund II: $300M closed Oct 2024). Notable govtech investment includes Carbyne - next-generation 911 and emergency response platform - which was acquired by Axon in November 2025 for $625M. Cox Enterprises is also the majority acquirer of OpenGov ($1.8B, 2024), giving Socium strategic alignment with govtech through its parent. Portfolio also includes health, enterprise software, and AI companies.
funding_detail: Cox Enterprises-backed evergreen fund; $300M Fund II (Oct 2024); $600M+ total committed

name: Weatherford Capital (Will Weatherford)
description: Family-owned PE firm founded in 2015 by former Florida House Speaker Will Weatherford. Seven govtech platform investments since inception including PayIt (digital government payments), OpenGov ($1.8B exit to Cox Enterprises, 2024), SOMA Global (public safety), and BusPatrol (school bus safety). Closed $300M Fund II in 2025. Deep government relationships - rooted in Weatherford's legislative background - as a core value-add for portfolio companies navigating procurement.
funding_detail: Family-owned PE; $300M Fund II closed 2025; $1B+ AUM across two funds

name: Annie E. Casey Foundation
description: Major funder of Georgetown Beeck Center. Focus on child welfare, juvenile justice, and family economic success; all areas where government delivery capacity is critical. Funds community-based organizations and government agencies improving child/family outcomes through data and technology.

name: Arnold Ventures
description: Funds evidence-based government reform including Results for America and government performance initiatives. Focus on criminal justice, health, evidence-based implementation.

name: Ballmer Group (Steve & Connie Ballmer)
description: Funds data-driven systems change for economic mobility. Key funder of GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact. Supports USAFacts (gov data transparency platform Steve Ballmer personally launched). Large-scale state partnerships - $1B+ commitment to WA state early childhood. Focus on evidence-based government, workforce development, and using data to improve government services.
funding_detail: Steve Ballmer personal wealth (fmr. Microsoft CEO)

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies: Government Innovation
description: Major funder of city-level government innovation. Funds Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative, Bloomberg Center for Cities, What Works Cities (via Results for America), Data-Smart City Solutions, i-teams.
funding_detail: Bloomberg LP profits; Michael Bloomberg personal wealth

name: Blue Meridian Partners
description: Funder collaborative housed at Edna McConnell Clark Foundation that finds and scales solutions for economic mobility. Major Ballmer Group partner. Funds organizations at the intersection of nonprofit service delivery and government systems change. Relevant because many grantees work directly with government agencies on benefits delivery, workforce development, and child welfare systems.
funding_detail: Ballmer Group, Sergey Brin Family Foundation, Edna McConnell Clark Foundation + others; grants-based, not equity

name: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI)
description: LLC blending grants and investments. Funded FUSE Corps. Community program supports housing, health, and economic development in San Mateo County/Bay Area. Note: CZI significantly restructured in Feb 2025 - cut social advocacy funding, DEI teams, and shifted focus to AI in science and education. State capacity relevance is narrower now than pre-2025.
funding_detail: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan personal wealth; operates as LLC

name: Craig Newmark Philanthropies
description: Founded by craigslist founder. Major funder of Aspen Policy Academy / Tech Policy Hub since its founding. Supports cybersecurity, trustworthy journalism, and public interest technology pipeline. Pragmatic, hands-on funder with focus on infrastructure for civic tech.

name: Data.org
description: Nonprofit building the field of data for social impact. Capacity Accelerator Network provides training and resources for organizations using data to improve public services. Inclusive Growth and Recovery Challenge funds data-driven solutions.
funding_detail: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth + philanthropic

name: Democracy Fund (Omidyar Group)
description: Nonpartisan foundation focused on effective and accountable government as one of four pillars. Funds congressional modernization orgs (POPVOX Foundation, Lincoln Network), government transparency, and legislative branch capacity-building. $200+ grants/year. Doubling down on democracy defense in 2025-2026.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: Emerson Collective (Laurene Powell Jobs)
description: LLC (~$28B AUM) blending VC, philanthropy, and advocacy. Invested in OpenGov (pre-acquisition). Education reform (XQ Institute, College Track) and immigration policy are core verticals where EC works to reshape government systems. Founded Chicago CRED (gun violence intervention with government) and E Pluribus Unum (civic engagement in the South). Strong state and local policy advocacy capacity.
funding_detail: Powell Jobs personal wealth; Waverley Street Foundation committed $3.5B over 10 years

name: Ford Foundation
description: Major funder of public interest technology ecosystem. Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds Coding it Forward, FUSE Corps, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, Ash Center endowment, PIT Infrastructure Fund.

name: Gates Foundation
description: Funds GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact. Supports government data capacity for public health and education policy. K-12 and public health data systems work often intersects with state/local government capacity. Large-scale but government modernization is a secondary rather than primary focus.

name: Google.org
description: Google's philanthropic arm. Funded Decoded Futures AI capacity-building for NYC nonprofits ($1M grant). Supports AI for social good, digital skills training, and civic technology projects. Corporate partner for government AI pilots (e.g., Seattle, Boston traffic optimization).

name: Hewlett Foundation
description: Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds TechCongress, public interest technology infrastructure, and government performance programs.

name: Irvine Foundation (James Irvine Foundation)
description: California-focused funder. Supports FUSE Corps. Focus on economic and political inclusion in California; funds orgs that strengthen civic participation and government responsiveness at state and local levels.

name: Knight Foundation
description: Invests in civic engagement, data-driven governance, and smart city strategies. $4M+ investment in 8 orgs using tech/data to strengthen public services. Funds Harvard Data-Smart City Solutions, GovEx/JHU, San Jose AI partnerships, and Knight Emerging City Champions fellowship (micro-grants for young civic innovators in 8 Knight resident communities). Focus on mid-size US cities.

name: Luminate (Omidyar Group)
description: Global foundation focused on civic empowerment, data and digital rights, financial transparency, and independent media. Funds orgs working on government transparency, open data, and citizen participation. Spun out of Omidyar Network's Governance & Citizen Engagement initiative in 2018.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: MacArthur Foundation
description: Major funder of Civic Consulting Alliance ($6M+ since 2003). Supports government accountability, criminal justice reform, and community development orgs that work with local government. Also funds Data & Society and investigative journalism that surfaces government capacity issues.

name: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth / Mastercard Impact Fund
description: Corporate philanthropy arm. Co-funds PIT-UN with Ford and Hewlett. Funds data.org and data-for-social-impact initiatives. Supports government digital inclusion and financial access programs.

name: New Profit
description: Pioneer venture philanthropy fund investing in social entrepreneurs tackling civic engagement and government service delivery. In 2024 invested $2.6M across 24 organizations. Build Investments provide $1.5M multi-year unrestricted grants paired with deal partners. Portfolio includes public service pipeline orgs like Latinas Represent.

name: NextLadder Ventures
description: $1B+ initiative launched July 2025 by Ballmer Group, Gates Foundation, Stand Together, Valhalla Foundation, and John Overdeck. Invests in entrepreneurs building tech-enabled solutions helping low-income Americans navigate government systems and economic barriers. Uses a mix of grants, equity, and revenue-based financing over a 15-year horizon. Relevant to state capacity as it funds the interface layer between government benefits systems and residents.
funding_detail: $1B+ committed across founding coalition over 15 years; mix of grants, equity, and revenue-based financing

name: Open Philanthropy
description: Major funder of Niskanen Center (state capacity work) and immigration reform advocacy. Research-driven grantmaking. AI governance and policy is growing focus area. Funds GiveDirectly and evidence-based policy research that intersects with government delivery.
funding_detail: Cari Tuna and Dustin Moskovitz (Facebook co-founder)

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and orgs advancing responsible AI and data use in public sector.

name: Pivotal Ventures (Melinda French Gates)
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and pathways for underrepresented technologists in government.

name: Public Interest Technology Infrastructure Fund (PIT Fund)
description: Pooled grantmaking vehicle housed at New Venture Fund. Dedicated to building the PIT ecosystem; funds talent pipeline orgs like Coding it Forward ($550K), Govern for America, #BlackTechFutures ($250K), AAAS AI fellowships ($250K), PIT hubs ($200K each), and Data & Society. Funded by Ford, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal, Schmidt Futures.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal Ventures, Schmidt Futures

name: Raikes Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT-UN. Founded by Jeff Raikes (fmr. Microsoft exec, fmr. Gates Foundation CEO). Supports education, youth development, and public interest technology pipeline programs.

name: Robin Hood Foundation
description: NYC's largest local poverty-fighting philanthropy. Seeded Decoded Futures AI capacity-building for nonprofits delivering public services.

name: Rockefeller Foundation
description: Launched AI Readiness Project (Nov 2025) expanding to all 50 states. Funds state/local government AI capacity-building and digital inclusion.

name: Salesforce Foundation / Salesforce.org
description: Funds Decoded Futures. Provides technology grants and discounted CRM to nonprofits delivering public services. Power of Us program provides 10 free Salesforce licenses to nonprofits. Increasingly relevant as governments and their nonprofit partners adopt Salesforce for case management.

name: Schmidt Futures
description: Philanthropic initiative (Eric & Wendy Schmidt) making grants and investments at intersection of talent and technology. Funded Social Safety Net Product Studio, USDR, FAS, PIT-UN, benefits access modernization.
funding_detail: Schmidt family wealth; operates as LLC

name: Siegel Family Endowment
description: Committed $20M to PIT ecosystem. Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, New America PIT.

name: Valhalla Foundation
description: Philanthropy focused on measurable improvement in children's lives through early childhood development, K-12 education, and data science. Co-founder of NextLadder Ventures. Invests in data-driven approaches to improving government-run systems particularly in education and child welfare. Collaborative philanthropy model emphasizing cross-funder coordination.

name: Aspen Policy Academy (fmr. Aspen Tech Policy Hub)
description: S&T Policy Training (3-week intensive), TELI exec program (5-week, 150+ alumni), Primer, and short courses training STEM professionals on policy impact.
funding_detail: Craig Newmark Philanthropies, Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative
description: Executive education for mayors and senior city officials. Summer fellowships for Harvard grad students. Innovation track with Centre for Public Impact.

name: Civic Tech Institute (Equitech Futures)
description: 10-week fully funded cohort program training early-career professionals in data science, AI, and civic innovation. Certificate + 1-year alumni mentorship.

name: Decoded Futures (Tech:NYC Foundation)
description: AI capacity-building for NYC nonprofits delivering public services. Cohort-based AI training, industry tech mentors, prototyping support, and grants ($5K-$100K/org).
funding_detail: Robin Hood, Google.org, Salesforce, OpenAI, Altman Foundation, AWS

name: InnovateUS
description: Delivers free, self-paced and live digital skills training (data, design, innovation, procurement) to public servants at all levels.

name: Partnership for Public Service: AI Government Leadership Program
description: Cohort-based program training federal leaders on AI strategy, implementation, and governance. Expanded to two cohorts in 2025 with virtual option. Also runs AI Onboarding Program for 55 early-career federal technologists. AI intern cohort with Maryland.

name: Agile Six
description: Public benefit corporation delivering human-centered digital services to federal agencies. Primary focus on VA digital services and benefits delivery, CDC pandemic readiness, and CMS Medicare modernization. Fully remote, values-driven culture.

name: Bloom Works
description: Digital services consultancy delivering user research, service design, engineering, and content strategy to government agencies. Focus on healthcare.gov and social services modernization. Woman-owned small business.

name: Center for Civic Futures (CCF) / AI Readiness Project
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit running the AI Readiness Project. Convenes State Chief AI Officer Community of Practice (30+ states, expanding to 50). Government AI Knowledge Hub launching 2026. Structured pilots for responsible AI in public service.
funding_detail: Rockefeller Foundation ($500K+ for AI Readiness); philanthropic grants

name: Civic Consulting Alliance
description: Chicago-based nonprofit (est. 1985) providing $15-30M/year in pro bono consulting to city and county government. Mobilizes corporate partners (BCG, Deloitte, McKinsey, etc.) for systems-level projects on economic development, education, safety, and health. $200M+ total investment facilitated.
funding_detail: MacArthur Foundation, corporate pro bono partners, philanthropic grants

name: CivicActions
description: Twenty years delivering digital services to federal and state agencies — open-source by default and outcomes-focused. Current portfolio includes healthcare.gov, medicare.gov, cms.gov, nsf.gov, and va.gov, with deep practice in agile delivery, user-centered design, accessibility compliance, DevSecOps, and responsible AI-enabled modernization.

name: Civilla
description: Nonprofit design studio dedicated to changing how public-serving institutions work. Human-centered design approach to redesigning government forms, processes, and services. Redesigned Michigan's public benefits application (recognized by Harvard Innovations in Government). Partners with Beeck Center.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants + earned revenue from government partnerships

name: Code for America
description: Leading civic tech nonprofit (15+ yrs). Builds digital tools and changes policies improving criminal justice, safety net, and tax systems. Hosts annual Summit.

name: Harvard Government Performance Lab (GPL)
description: Embeds full-time fellows in state/local government agencies for 12-36 month reform projects on child welfare, criminal justice, homelessness, housing, and procurement. 112 jurisdictions across 38 states. 278+ projects shifting $7B+ in government spending. Pro bono. Part of Harvard Kennedy School.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Rockefeller Foundation + Harvard Kennedy School

name: mRelief
description: Nonprofit building tools to simplify access to government benefits. Text and web-based screeners help residents determine eligibility for SNAP, Medicaid, and other programs. Grew out of Chi Hack Night. Partners with city governments and social service orgs.

name: Nava PBC
description: Public benefit corporation delivering agile software development, user-centered design, and cloud engineering to government agencies. Built Healthcare.gov fixes and VA.gov. ~200 employees focused exclusively on government digital services.

name: Partners for Public Good (PPG)
description: Independent nonprofit (launched Mar 2025) spun out of Harvard GPL's procurement research initiative after a decade of incubation. Helps state and local governments improve procurement, staffing, digital infrastructure, and budgeting. Runs Procurement Excellence Network (2,000+ government officials across all 50 states). $5.4B in public spending affected. 200+ local jurisdictions served.

name: Rockefeller Foundation: State AI Technical Assistance
description: Beyond grantmaking, Rockefeller directly provides strategic planning support and technical assistance to states on AI adoption. Funded Maryland Anthropic/Percepta partnership. Funds CCF AI Readiness Project. $18M+ in AI-related investments to date.

name: Skylight Digital
description: Digital government consultancy delivering agile procurement support, user-centered design, cloud/DevOps, and API-first architecture to federal agencies. HUBZone-certified small business.

name: U.S. Digital Response (USDR)
description: Matches 7,000+ volunteer technologists with governments needing pro bono technical assistance on digital services, procurement, and talent. 300+ projects. Runs Digital Service Champions Awards.

name: VotingWorks
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit building open-source, publicly owned voting machines and election auditing software. Only nonprofit building certified voting systems in the US. Deployed in multiple states.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants; nonprofit; only certified nonprofit voting system builder in US

name: 120Water
description: Platform helping municipalities manage water safety testing, lead service line inventories, and EPA compliance. Sells directly to water utilities and government agencies. Over 1,300 communities served. $43M raised.
funding_detail: $57.6M total raised; $43M Series B (Jan 2024) led by Edison Partners; 1,300+ communities served

name: Binti
description: Software for child welfare agencies managing foster care approvals, placements, and adoptions. Reduces paperwork and accelerates family matching. Sells directly to county and state child welfare departments.

name: Biobot Analytics
description: Wastewater epidemiology platform helping government public health agencies monitor disease prevalence at population level. MIT-origin. Contracts with CDC and local health departments.
funding_detail: Y Combinator + $20M Series A (2022); $30M+ total raised; CDC contracts

name: CivicReach
description: AI-powered government customer service platform automating resident inquiries and improving service delivery across multiple channels.
funding_detail: $310K raised; NC Tweener Fund, Flybridge, NC Idea; founded 2024

name: CiviForm
description: Open-source unified benefits application platform built by and for governments. Developed by the City of Seattle with Google.org Fellows and Exygy during the pandemic; now adopted by Seattle, Charlotte NC, Bloomington IN, the State of Arkansas, and Miami-Dade County. Lets residents reuse their information to apply for multiple benefit programs at once, cutting average application time from 30 to 7 minutes. Governments use a no-code interface to author and manage program applications without vendor dependency - the codebase is collectively owned and governed by the adopting governments. Named Time Magazine Best Inventions of 2025. 50,000+ applications processed in Seattle alone. Stewarded by Exygy (Certified B Corp) with Google.org grant funding.
funding_detail: Google.org grant funding to Exygy; free and open-source for adopting governments; Seed/Early stage

name: Cyvl.ai
description: Vehicle-mounted sensors and AI software enabling governments to monitor and manage physical infrastructure. Transforms any vehicle into a data collection platform for road conditions, signage, and urban planning. Sells to DOTs and municipal public works departments.
funding_detail: $9.2M total raised; $6M round (Mar 2024) led by Companyon Ventures; DOT and municipal clients

name: Daupler
description: Response management platform for public works and utility departments replacing clipboard-based workflows with digital dispatch and field operations tools. Mobile-first interface for managing service requests and work orders. One of the fastest-growing govtech companies by traffic and employment growth (2023-2025).
funding_detail: Undisclosed early-stage funding; high growth trajectory 2023-2025

name: Elucd
description: Near-real-time survey platform measuring how residents perceive government and public safety. Data-driven community trust analytics sold directly to police departments and city governments.
funding_detail: Govtech Fund + Luminate + others; $120K+ disclosed; seed stage

name: Findhelp (fmr. Aunt Bertha)
description: Social care technology platform (est. 2010) connecting residents to government and community benefit programs through a unified search and referral system. Partners directly with state and local government agencies to build resources databases, manage closed-loop referrals, and track outcomes. Notable contracts include Missouri DESE (250,000+ families), state Medicaid agencies, and county health departments. Passes capacity test: gives government workers and residents better tools to navigate and deliver existing benefit programs - augments caseworkers rather than replacing them.
funding_detail: Raised $25M+ total; Series B and beyond; B Corp certified public benefit corporation; government and health system contracts

name: GovWell
description: Software for streamlining government permitting, licensing, and code enforcement processes. Unlike PermitFlow (which sells to contractors), GovWell sells directly to local government agencies including building departments, planning/zoning, fire, and public works.
funding_detail: $6.5M total raised; seed round (2024) from Work-Bench, Bienville Capital, Fractal Software; 30+ states

name: Hazel Analytics
description: Platform aggregating public health inspection data (restaurants, pools, childcare) across jurisdictions for health departments. Helps government environmental health agencies prioritize inspections and track compliance. Used by multiple state and county health departments.
funding_detail: Undisclosed early-stage funding; multiple state and county health department deployments

name: Holly
description: AI-powered platform modernizing government hiring. Automates job description creation with 45,000+ templates, provides real-time salary benchmarking, and reduces government hiring cycles that average 135 days. Addresses ~1M vacant government positions nationwide.
funding_detail: J2 Ventures + early-stage investors; undisclosed total; 45,000+ job description templates

name: PayIt
description: Digital payment and services platform enabling residents to transact with government (DMV, property tax, utilities) via mobile. Revenue model based on transaction fees, often at no cost to the agency. $190M+ raised.
funding_detail: Insight Partners, Weatherford Capital; $190M+ total raised; transaction fee model

name: Peregrine Technologies
description: Real-time data intelligence platform for public safety and government agencies, enabling state and local governments to unify siloed data for decision-making across law enforcement, emergency response, fraud detection, and health services. Serves agencies protecting 80M+ Americans. Tripled revenue each of the prior three years. High-profile deployments include coordinating multi-agency operations at Super Bowl LIX. Passes capacity test: gives government agencies better real-time intelligence to make decisions - does not replace government personnel.
funding_detail: $220M total raised; $190M Series C (Mar 2025) led by Sequoia Capital at $2.5B valuation; prior $30M Series B (May 2024)

name: Polco
description: Community engagement and survey platform built for local government. Powers the National Community Survey (NCS) used by 600+ jurisdictions. Provides benchmarking data, resident polling, and budget simulation tools for city managers and elected officials.
funding_detail: National Research Center merger; $15M+ raised; 600+ jurisdictions using National Community Survey

name: Promise
description: Modernizes government payment and collections systems, helping agencies recover revenue while giving residents flexible, humane payment options. Sells directly to government billing departments.
funding_detail: Y Combinator (S19) + follow-on; $30M+ total raised; government payment modernization

name: SimpliGov
description: No-code workflow automation platform purpose-built for government, digitizing paper-based processes like licensing, permits, HR onboarding, and constituent requests. Clients include federal agencies and state/local governments.
funding_detail: JMI Equity strategic growth investment (Jan 2025; undisclosed amount); state and local workflow automation leader

name: Zencity
description: AI-powered community insights platform helping local governments understand resident sentiment, measure service satisfaction, and make data-driven decisions. Acquired UK-based Commonplace. Used by 350+ cities including NYC, Phoenix, and Nashville.
funding_detail: TLV Partners, M12 (Microsoft); $30M+ raised; 350+ city clients including NYC, Phoenix, Nashville

name: AI Now Institute of Technology
description: Independent policy research institute (est. 2017 at NYU; fully independent since 2022) studying the social implications of AI with a focus on power concentration, public accountability, and government use of AI. Annual Landscape Report is a field-defining publication on AI governance. Leadership advised the FTC on AI in 2021-22. Research covers government use of AI in benefits systems, hiring, criminal justice, and public services - making it directly relevant to state capacity accountability. Explicitly refuses corporate tech funding to maintain independence. 2025 Landscape Report: "Artificial Power" focused on reclaiming public control over AI trajectory. Funded by Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Omidyar Network, Luminate.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Omidyar Network, Luminate; no corporate tech industry funding

name: Aspen Institute
description: Nonpartisan forum for values-based leadership. Relevant programs include Aspen Policy Academy (see Training segment), Aspen Digital (tech policy), and various governance convenings. Broader than state capacity but significant convening power at leadership level.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; major foundation support; event revenue

name: Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC)
description: Centrist think tank founded by former Senate majority leaders from both parties. Governance program focuses on congressional capacity, executive branch management, and government modernization. Technology project examines AI governance and digital government policy.
funding_detail: Bipartisan philanthropic base; foundation and corporate support

name: Brookings: Center for Technology Innovation
description: Policy research on AI governance, digital government, tech talent, and government modernization. Congressional testimony.

name: Building State Capability (BSC) - Harvard Kennedy School
description: Applied research program at Harvard Kennedy School led by Prof. Matt Andrews, pioneering the Problem Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA) methodology for escaping government capability traps. Foundational scholarship on why government reforms fail (isomorphic mimicry, premature load-bearing) and how to build real implementation capacity. Has trained 4,850+ practitioners in 157 countries including US state and local officials. Offers online courses, executive education, and PDIA coaching. Most directly relevant academic program to the core question of how governments build implementation capacity.
funding_detail: Harvard Kennedy School endowment + earned revenue from executive education

name: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
description: Bipartisan national security think tank. Technology and National Security program researches AI, emerging tech, and defense innovation. [NOTE: Primarily defense-focused. State capacity relevance is limited to where defense tech/AI governance intersects with broader government modernization.]
funding_detail: Broad bipartisan donor base; foundation and government grants

name: Center for Democracy and Technology (CDT)
description: Nonpartisan 501(c)(3) (est. 1994) promoting democratic values by shaping technology policy with a focus on individual rights. CDT AI Governance Lab (launched May 2023, director Miranda Bogen) is the most state capacity-relevant unit - advises policymakers on AI auditing, safety, and accountability; publishes technical guidance on bias measurement, AI documentation, fairness assessments, and government use of AI in benefits, education, and law enforcement. Works directly with federal agencies and regulators. Hosted fellowships for researchers on algorithmic fairness and AI safety. In 2024 the Lab analyzed open foundation model risks with Stanford HAI and published reports on AI assurance and action-taking AI agents.
funding_detail: Foundation-funded; Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, and others; no corporate tech funding

name: Center for Tribal Digital Sovereignty (ASU / NCAI)
description: First and only center in the US dedicated to helping tribal governments build digital sovereignty plans. Launched June 2024 as a partnership between the American Indian Policy Institute (AIPI) at ASU Law and the National Congress of American Indians. Serves all 574 federally recognized Tribal Nations. Provides research, capacity-building support, and policy advocacy. Publishes AI governance frameworks for tribal contexts (Feb 2026). Co-hosts the annual Wiring the Rez conference (227 participants from 44 Tribal nations in 2025). Seed funding from Ford Foundation and Google.org. Acts as clearinghouse for tribal digital sovereignty resources - broadband governance, data sovereignty, spectrum management, and tribal tech codes.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation + Google.org seed funding; ASU and NCAI foundational support; seeking additional philanthropic partners

name: Centre for Public Impact (CPI)
description: Global not-for-profit providing government reimagining consulting, adaptive leadership coaching, and legitimacy frameworks.

name: Council of State Governments (CSG)
description: Founded 1933 - the nation's only nonpartisan organization serving all three branches of state government. Publishes the annual Book of the States (comprehensive statistical reference on state government) and Capitol Ideas magazine. New CSG 50-State Scan policy research series (2025) examines top priorities including government performance and reform. CSG Justice Center develops research-driven criminal justice reform strategies. Six regional offices support state legislators, governors, and judicial officials with research, TA, and peer exchange.
funding_detail: State appropriations (population-based dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: Data & Society
description: Research institute studying social implications of data and AI. Public Technology Leadership Collaborative connects tech experts with government leaders.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Foundation for American Innovation
description: Think tank advancing technology-government interface with senior fellows and policy work on AI governance, innovation policy, and institutional reform.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center
description: Provides technical assistance, communities of practice, and practitioner training on digital government, data governance, and AI for state/local agencies. Runs Digital Government Hub.
funding_detail: Georgetown + Annie E. Casey Foundation, Bloomberg, others

name: Governing Institute
description: Research and events arm of Governing (media platform for state/local leaders). Produces research on government performance, digital transformation, and AI adoption. Partners with Center for Digital Government on Digital States/Cities surveys.

name: Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA)
description: National professional association of 30,000+ state, provincial, and local government finance officers (est. 1906). Publishes the authoritative Governmental Accounting, Auditing, and Financial Reporting guide (GAAFR/"Blue Book") and Government Finance Review magazine. Research and Consulting Center is the market leader in helping local governments procure ERP and financial systems - has assisted 450+ governments with system selection and contract negotiation. Runs best practice award programs (CAFR, budget awards) and leadership training. 1-year Research Fellows program for recent UChicago graduates.
funding_detail: Member dues + conference revenue + consulting fees + publication sales

name: GovEx / Johns Hopkins Centers for Civic Impact
description: Bloomberg Center for Government Excellence at Johns Hopkins. Provides technical assistance, coaching, and training to help cities use data, analytics, and AI. Runs City Data Alliance and GovEx Academy (online courses). Worked with 140+ cities. CDOs-in-Residence program.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Ballmer Group, Knight Foundation, Gates Foundation + JHU

name: Harvard Ash Center for Democratic Governance and Innovation
description: Leading academic center for government innovation and democratic governance at Harvard Kennedy School. $50M Ford Foundation endowment. Programs include: Innovations in American Government Awards (recognizing excellence in state/local government since 1985); Data-Smart City Solutions (Bloomberg-funded, covering city data and AI); Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation (technology and democratic institutions); and Harvard Project on American Indian Economic Development. Houses the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative executive education program.
funding_detail: $50M Ford Foundation endowment + Bloomberg Philanthropies ($32M for City Leadership Initiative) + Harvard Kennedy School

name: IBM Center for the Business of Government
description: Independent research center (est. 1998 as PricewaterhouseCoopers Endowment; acquired by IBM 2002) funding third-party practitioner-focused research on public management at federal, state, and local levels. Publishes 25+ reports per year on digital modernization, AI adoption, workforce, procurement, and service delivery. 2024-25 publications include GenAI for state government, AI-powered procurement, federal workforce transformation, and reducing administrative burden. Hosts forums, radio program, and maintains practitioner fellows. Led by Executive Director Dan Chenok (former career federal CIO executive).

name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF)
description: Nonpartisan science and tech policy think tank. Research on government IT modernization, AI policy, and digital infrastructure. Published 'After DOGE: Trump's Chance to Modernize.'

name: Manhattan Institute
description: Center-right think tank focused on urban policy and public-sector reform. Governance program promotes transparency, accountability, and evidence-based reforms. Published 'Digital Transformation: Wiring the Responsive City.' City Journal magazine covers urban governance and innovation. Cities Director John Ketcham leads governance work.
funding_detail: Conservative philanthropic base; individual and foundation donors

name: Mercatus Center (George Mason University)
description: University-based research center. Regulatory reform, permitting modernization, and government process improvement research. Published influential work on regulatory accumulation and its effects on government capacity. Technology policy program.
funding_detail: George Mason University + Koch-affiliated and broad donor base

name: MIT GOV/LAB
description: Research lab studying government innovation, political accountability, and institutional design using field experiments and design thinking.

name: NASCIO (National Association of State Chief Information Officers)
description: The primary peer network, research body, and voice for state CIOs. Conducts the annual State CIO Survey (51 state/territory responses in 2025) and publishes State CIO Top 10 Priorities. Partners with McKinsey, EY, and Deloitte on major research initiatives including GenAI adoption, cybersecurity, and data quality. Hosts two annual conferences in DC and a fall gathering. Produces the definitive annual mapping of state technology priorities. NASCIO State IT Recognition Awards annually highlight the most innovative state IT programs.
funding_detail: State membership dues + corporate associate program + conference revenue

name: National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA)
description: Congressionally chartered. Convenes expert panels studying federal agency management, organizational design, and institutional effectiveness.

name: National Civic League
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit (est. 1894) promoting civic engagement and government innovation. All-America City Award (oldest community recognition in US). Research on collaborative governance, civic infrastructure, and democratic innovation.

name: National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL)
description: Bipartisan organization serving all 7,500+ state legislators and legislative staff across all 50 states, commonwealths, and territories. Produces nonpartisan policy research, technical assistance, and legislative tracking across every major issue area including technology, AI (tracked 450+ bills in 23 AI categories in 2024), cybersecurity, broadband, and digital government. Annual Legislative Summit and Fall Forum. Budget of ~$40M. Dual headquarters in Denver and DC.
funding_detail: State legislative appropriations (member dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: National League of Cities (NLC)
description: Membership organization and research body representing 19,000+ cities, towns, and villages - serving 90%+ of Americans. Annual State of Cities report (12th edition 2025) surveys mayors on top priorities. Publishes State and Local Fiscal Facts and digital government research. Partners with Beeck Center on digital services guidance for local governments. Hosts annual City Summit and State of GovTech conference (with CivStart) for city CIOs and elected officials. Advocates for federal policy supporting city capacity, broadband, and AI governance.
funding_detail: City membership dues + foundation grants + federal grants

name: New America: Public Interest Technology
description: PIT program: fellowships, The Commons (procurement research), policy research. Co-convenes PIT University Network (PIT-UN): 63 institutions, $16M+ deployed.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: NGA Center for Best Practices
description: The only R&D organization in the nation that directly serves governors. Develops innovative policy solutions through five divisions (economic/workforce, education, environment/energy/transportation, health, homeland security).
